what: Atmagir, a mahant of Hardwar, leased the Dun forest dues in 1839 for Rs. 33,500 (later said to receive c. Rs. 80,000 a year); the name in -gir suggests a Giri Daśanāmī but order is not stated
quote: in 1839 the forest dues wore again leased for five years: on this occasion to Atmagir, a mahant of Hardwar, for Rs. 33,500.

what: Gurudwara of the Udasis founded by Ram Rai, built 1699; mahant elected from the chelas of the last mahant; Holi/Sangat fair of 8,000-10,000
quote: The temple or Gurudwara of the Udasis, the sect of religious ascctics founded by Ram Raj, thuir Guru, was built in 1699 A.D. and is the only object of historical interest.

what: Mahant Lachhman Das holds the temple endowment: Dehra Khas and other villages revenue-free, nominal revenue Rs. 11,289, plus villages in the Dun and Tehri; most important proprietor in the district
quote: The most important landed proprietor from the statistical point of view is Mahant Lachhman Das of the Guru Ram Rai temple in Dehra, He holds, as the endowment of the temple, in Dehra itself land paying a nominal revenue of Rs, 11,289.

what: Ten-day Sangat fair from 1 Chait at the Ram Rai temple; pilgrims go on to Hardwar Kumbh
quote: A fair lasting ten days, and called Sangat, commences on the Ist Chait, and on the 6th the ceremony of hoisting a new flag

what: An estate now owned partly by the mahant of Rikhikesh (order not stated)

what: Town swarms with sadhus fed by free kitchens at the Panjab Kshetra (Sikh) and the dharmsala of Ram Nath Kali Kamliwala
